question.problem:
Find the second-degree Taylor polynomial ${P}_{2}(x)$ of $f(x)=\frac{1}{1-x}$ about $x=\frac{1}{2}.$

${P}_{2}(x)=$
{{field-1}}$\,+$
{{field-2}}$(x-\frac{1}{2})\,+$
{{field-3}}${(x-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}$
question.worked_solution:
To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=\frac{1}{2},$ we plug $a=\frac{1}{2}$ into the general formula to give

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(\frac{1}{2})+{f}^{′}(\frac{1}{2})(x-\frac{1}{2})+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2}){(x-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}.
$$

So, we need to work out $f(\frac{1}{2}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{1}{2}),$ and ${f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{1}{1-x} & ⟹ &  & f(\frac{1}{2}) & =2 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{(1-x)^{2}} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\frac{1}{2}) & =4 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{2}{(1-x)^{3}} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2}) & =16\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(\frac{1}{2}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{1}{2}),$ and ${f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2})$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =2+4(x-\frac{1}{2})+16\cdot \frac{1}{2}{(x-\frac{1}{2})}^{2} \\  & =2+4(x-\frac{1}{2})+8{(x-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
